assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides and single-molecule/cluster detection turned DNA reading into a massively parallel chemical process, cutting cost by orders of magnitude and reshaping biology and medicine. The principle is clear and quantitative (read cost and throughput scaling), and the generative impact is exactly the kind of 'unforeseen opportunities' a broad citation can explain.
assessment.attribution: The Cambridge chemistry of Balasubramanian and Klenerman (Solexa) is the clear core of the chemical invention. Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based emulsion PCR platform), Mayer and Ju contributed parallel or competing approaches; a two-person prize is defensible but leaves the 454 and other platforms' credit contested.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of near-universal adoption and independent confirmation; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry rather than biotechnology or physiology/medicine.
Credit split with Rothberg and others on the first commercial parallel platforms is unresolved.
I am relying on my general knowledge of the history and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues opens an entirely new pharmacological modality: induced proximity that removes a target rather than inhibiting it. The mechanistic insight that thalidomide-type drugs act through cereblon unified an old clinical puzzle with a general design principle.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (PROTAC concept and development) and Handa (cereblon as thalidomide target, with Ito) form a natural trio covering the concept and the molecular-glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray and others made decisive later refinements (VHL ligands, degrader design) and could be argued in; Sakamoto and Kim contributed the early PROTAC work.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in late clinical trials and lenalidomide-class glues are approved, but the first PROTAC approval is still pending, so recognition is somewhat early on the therapeutic side.
uncertainties: Clinical validation of PROTACs specifically is incomplete.
Distinguishing original discovery (PROTAC) from later refinements and glues complicates the prize configuration.
Credit among Sakamoto, Kim, Ciulli and Gray is disputed or unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors perform direct chemical conversion of one base to another at a programmed genomic site without double-strand breaks, a genuinely new capability built on a deaminase chemistry idea. Clinical use in correcting disease alleles shows clear generative potential beyond nuclease editing.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the intellectual leader; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, requiring directed evolution of a tRNA deaminase) made the two decisive inventions. Nishida and Kondo reported an independent deaminase-fusion editing concept that complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Only about a decade old, but independently reproduced widely and now entering clinics; the CRISPR prize in 2020 makes a follow-on timing question plausible, though the chemistry is distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may make the committee prefer to wait.
Clinical evidence is still limited in scale.
Independent early work by Nishida and Kondo affects fair attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Passing single polynucleotides through a protein or solid-state pore and reading them by ionic current blockades is a beautiful single-molecule physics measurement that became a deployed sequencing technology with long reads and direct RNA and modification readout. It combines a clear principle with practical capability.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer demonstrated translocation and detection in 1996; Akeson led the control and enzyme-ratcheting that enabled base resolution; Bayley engineered the pore and chemistry. Branton (and I believe Bayley) are deceased, which constrains the credited set; I am uncertain of their status.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices are in routine use and reproduced independently, so maturity is good, though accuracy and throughput are still maturing.
uncertainties: Status of Branton and Bayley should be confirmed, as it constrains eligible laureates.
The citation might be read as physics or biotechnology rather than chemistry.
Distinguishing the 1996 proof of principle from later enzyme-ratcheting engineering is delicate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments links polymer physics to cell biology and reframed how we think about intracellular organization. It resonates strongly with a physicist's view of a general underlying principle.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's P granule work (2009) is the foundational observation; Rosen's multivalency work on signaling and Pappu's sequence-grammar theory add key principles. The three-way set is defensible but excludes Pappu and Mittag, whose conceptual contributions are sizeable.
assessment.maturity: Very influential but still debated: physiological relevance, definition of condensates and in-cell measurement are contested, so the interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Skepticism about in vivo phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology.
Credit among the five names is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and ion dynamics in a single fictitious-dynamics scheme, making ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and reactions routine. It is an original, elegant, quantitative method with lasting impact across chemistry, physics and materials.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is clearly the decisive contribution, a clean two-person attribution. Parrinello also appears under metadynamics, which could be considered together.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of widespread use; fully mature, though the theoretical-methods area was recognized recently (2013 multiscale models) which could argue against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2013 prize for multiscale modelling.
Whether the committee wants to recognize a computational method this year.
Possible grouping with metadynamics changes the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in a decade, with defect-tolerant electronic properties that raise fundamental physical questions. This is a striking capability jump in solar energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park and Snaith/Seok drove the solid-state breakthroughs (2012); Grätzel and Kanatzidis also contributed. Fair attribution among six names is hard.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently confirmed, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercialization are not settled.
Credit split among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok, Grätzel and Kanatzidis is contentious.
Primarily a materials and device physics story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled safe, effective in vivo delivery of siRNA and mRNA, making the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and RNA therapeutics possible. The impact is enormous and concrete, rooted in lipid physical chemistry and self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the lipid-nanoparticle systems work with collaborators (Madden, Hope, MacLachlan); Langer and Anderson developed other delivery materials. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized the mRNA modification side, so credit for the delivery chemistry is separate but potentially entangled.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; timing is reasonable, though the Medicine 2023 prize may make the committee view the area as already honored.
uncertainties: Possible perception of overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.
Allocation among Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan and Anderson is unresolved.
Single-laureate choice reflects the lead contribution I recall and is not independently verified.
